title: k-nearest neighbours, naive Bayes and support vector machines

videos.script: Three ideas, each older than most of the people using them. {{three}} The first: to predict a new subscriber, find the fifteen most like them, and let them vote. That is nearest neighbours. {{knn}} Measure similarity in raw units, and the price decides everything. Scale the columns, and the same model makes eighty times the money. {{scale}} The second: count the words in a review. Complaints say bruised and late. The rest say ripe and lovely. Naive Bayes multiplies that evidence, and gets ninety-two per cent right. {{bayes}} It is also wildly overconfident, and you will see why. {{overconfident}} The third: draw the widest possible street between two classes, and let a kernel bend it. That is a support vector machine. {{svm}} At the end, four models draw their boundaries on the same points. A line. A wobble. A curve. {{boundaries}} And on the churn table, none of them wins. Which is why the next two lessons are about trees. {{end}}
